issues: Sheets 4-6: the core event never happens; the balls never visibly fall from the top of the frame, nothing lands on a floor (no ground line), and the only motion is a slight shift and a dashed line at 10.7 to 12 s, so the viewer never sees both balls hit together and the prediction has no payoff.

Sheets 1-3: the opening 6 s is a static frame of two small balls in the top-left corner with the rest of the frame empty; the balls are crowded to the left and top with no ground or drop-height reference, which wastes the vertical canvas and gives no sense of 'same height'.

Sheets 4-5: the prediction beat is weak; 'Which lands first?' sits as a title while a tiny grey '?' floats in the middle, with no way to choose or commit (no labels on the balls, no A/B choice, no countdown), and 2 s of silence at 8.0 to 10.0 s is a dead hold with no change.

Sheets 7-9: the explanation is not shown; 'Gravity speeds up every object at the same rate' has no acceleration cue, no velocity or equal arrows, no force diagram, and the balls just drift slowly down the frame; the ball and its faint green ghost trails are unrelated to the narration, and 'They land together' appears in huge yellow chalk at 12.47 s about 2 s after the narration said it, then vanishes.

Sheets 9-12: 'air resistance' is a large grey chalk label that covers the lower middle for 6 s while the narration says only air resistance can split them and barely matters; no demo of drag, no side by side, and the label is bigger than anything else so the key idea (why they land together) loses weight.

Sheets 1-12: bottom captions are tiny, thin, centred, and get recalculated in size at each caption change (e.g. 0.23 s versus 0.47 s, 2.23 s versus 2.47 s), so they pulse; they are too small for a phone and the bowling ball and tennis ball are not labelled at all.
Sheets 6, 11: abrupt layout jumps; the balls teleport from top to mid-frame between 12.0 and 14.0 s, and an unexplained dark ghost circle appears near the tennis ball at 11.97 s.
Sheet 12: the ending just holds on a static frame with no conclusion or reveal.
